correctness.rationale: For U_theta f=f o R_theta the exact second-order chain-rule matrix in the {f_xx,f_xy,f_yy} coordinates has pure-column abs sums 1+|cs| and mixed-column sum |c^2-s^2|+4|cs|, which dominates first-jet |c|+|s| and zeroth-order 1 for every c^2+s^2=1. The classical scalar planar Ornstein endpoint L1 non-inequality produces compactly supported smooth functions with the mixed derivative dominating pure second derivatives; shrinking spatial scale then suppresses L1 lower-order terms. Reverse triangle inequalities imply the mixed-column lower bound, giving norm 2|sin2theta|+|cos2theta|. The quarter-circle envelope attains sqrt5 precisely where |sin2theta|=2/sqrt5, yielding isometry angles and diagonal cusp. Independent exact rational-angle checks reproduced Hessian coefficients, column dominance and bound at 169 angles; infinite-dimensional lower bound requires the cited Ornstein theorem, not those checks.
